````math
## Appendix E The Price of Explainability for $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ Clustering

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

### E.1 Introduction

Clustering is a central topic in optimization, machine learning, and
algorithm design. Given $`n`$ points in $`\mathbb{R}^{d}`$ and a
parameter $`k`$, the $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ clustering problem asks to
partition the points into $`k`$ clusters with centers
$`\mathcal{U}=\{{\bm{\mu}}^{1},\ldots,{\bm{\mu}}^{k}\}`$ so as to
minimize

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\mathrm{cost}_{p}(\pi,\mathcal{U})=\sum_{{\bm{x}}\in\mathcal{X}}\|{\bm{x}}-\pi({\bm{x}})\|_{p}^{p},`$ |  | (8) |

where $`\pi({\bm{x}})`$ maps each point to its assigned center. The
cases $`p=1`$ ($`k`$-medians) and $`p=2`$ ($`k`$-means) are the most
extensively studied.

In the *explainable clustering* model of Dasgupta
et al. \[[3](#bibe.bib3)\], clusters are described by a *threshold
tree*: a binary decision tree where each internal node makes an
axis-aligned threshold cut $`x_{i}\leq\theta`$ and each leaf corresponds
to a cluster. This yields interpretable clusterings—each cluster is
described by a short sequence of feature thresholds. The *price of
explainability* is the worst-case ratio of the optimal explainable cost
to the optimal unrestricted cost.

##### Prior work.

Gupta, Pittu, Svensson, and Yuan \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\] gave a
comprehensive study for $`p\in\{1,2\}`$. For $`k`$-medians they proved
the price is exactly $`1+H_{k-1}=\Theta(\ln k)`$, via a tight analysis
of the Random Thresholds algorithm combined with matching lower bounds
from a hitting-set reduction. For $`k`$-means they proved the price is
$`O(k\ln\ln k)`$, improving the previous $`O(k\ln k)`$
bound \[[4](#bibe.bib4)\], and showed a lower bound of $`\Omega(k)`$
(from \[[6](#bibe.bib6)\]). They also proved that explainable
$`k`$-medians and $`k`$-means are hard to approximate better than
$`(\nicefrac{{1}}{{2}}-o(1))\ln k`$ unless $`P=NP`$. They noted that the
$`k`$-means ideas “extend to $`\ell_{p}`$ norms for $`p\geq 2`$” but
deferred the details to future work; this makes the present paper a
completion of their announced direction. Gamlath
et al. \[[6](#bibe.bib6)\] also noted in their NeurIPS 2021 paper
(Section 6, Open Problems) that their ideas should extend to higher
$`\ell_{p}`$ norms, but neither they nor GPSY23 published formal proofs
for $`p>2`$. The regime $`p>2`$ has therefore been noted as a natural
extension by multiple groups, but to our knowledge no complete proofs
have appeared.

We note that the $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ clustering objective studied here
(which raises each coordinate difference to the $`p`$-th power) is
distinct from the explainable $`k`$-medians problem under the
$`\ell_{p}`$ *norm* (which raises the $`\ell_{p}`$ norm to the first
power). The latter has been studied recently, including for general
finite $`p\geq 1`$ (see \[[8](#bibe.bib8)\] and NeurIPS 2025 work on
explainable $`k`$-medians under $`\ell_{p}`$ norms). Those results
operate in a different cost model and do not directly imply our bounds.

#### E.1.1 Our Results

We develop the detailed proof machinery for the price of explainability
in the $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ regime for $`p>2`$. While GPSY23 announced the
extension as forthcoming and GJPS21 noted it as an open direction, the
details—particularly the generalized $`D_{p}`$ distribution, the
stretch-vs-separation analysis via Hölder’s inequality for $`p>2`$, the
convexity-based induction closing, and the corrected close-pair
threshold—have not appeared in the literature. Our contribution is the
self-contained $`p>2`$ upper-bound proof
([Theorem E.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Theorem E.1 (Upper Bound for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, 𝑝>2). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale"));
the $`p=2`$ bound is a direct consequence of \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\]
([Corollary E.2](#A5.Thmtheorem2 "Corollary E.2 (Upper Bound for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, 𝑝=2). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")).

###### Theorem E.1 (Upper Bound for $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$, $`p>2`$).

For any $`p>2`$, the price of explainability for $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$
clustering is $`O(k^{p-1}\ln\ln k)`$. Specifically, given any reference
$`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ clustering, there exists a randomized algorithm that
outputs an explainable clustering with expected cost at most
$`O(k^{p-1}\ln\ln k)`$ times the reference cost.

###### Corollary E.2 (Upper Bound for $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$, $`p=2`$).

For $`p=2`$, the price of explainability for $`\ell_{2}^{2}`$ clustering
($`k`$-means) is $`O(k\ln\ln k)`$.

###### Proof.

This is the result of \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\] (their Theorem 1.2). We invoke
their sharper solo-cost analysis as the base case for $`p=2`$. ∎

###### Remark E.3 (Proof structure).

[Theorem E.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Theorem E.1 (Upper Bound for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, 𝑝>2). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")
is self-contained: the solo cost induction
([Lemma E.15](#A5.Thmtheorem15 "Lemma E.15 (Solo Cost). ‣ E.4.4 Solo Cut Analysis ‣ E.4 Upper Bound: 𝑂(𝑘^{𝑝-1}⁢lnln𝑘) ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale"))
closes via the convexity of $`t\mapsto t^{p-1}`$ and the Hölder-based
balance bound $`A_{p}(n)^{p-1}=O(n^{p-2})`$. For $`p=2`$, the same
induction does not close ($`A_{2}(n)=O(\ln n)`$ is too large); we
instead invoke the GPSY23 analysis \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\] as a base case.
The contribution of the present paper is concentrated in the $`p>2`$
machinery.

###### Conjecture E.4 (Lower Bound for $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$, $`p>2`$).

For any $`p>2`$ and $`k\geq 2`$, the price of explainability for
$`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ clustering is $`\Omega(k^{p-1})`$.

For $`p=2`$, the unconditional lower bound $`\Omega(k)`$ was proved by
Gamlath et al. \[[6](#bibe.bib6)\]. For $`p>2`$, the GJPS21
$`\Omega(k)`$ lower bound applies unconditionally: their construction
uses points on the Boolean hypercube $`\{0,1\}^{d}`$, where
$`\|x-y\|_{p}^{p}=\|x-y\|_{1}`$ for all $`p`$ (since each coordinate
difference is in $`\{0,1\}`$), so the same instance gives
$`\text{PoE}_{p}(k)\geq\Omega(k)`$ for all $`p\geq 2`$. However, this
only yields $`\Omega(k)`$, not the conjectured $`\Omega(k^{p-1})`$. We
prove that the $`\ell_{p}`$ stretch bound $`(k-1)^{p-1}`$ is tight
([Proposition E.16](#A5.Thmtheorem16 "Proposition E.16 (Tight Stretch). ‣ E.5 Stretch Tightness and Lower Bound Discussion ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")),
which provides suggestive evidence for
[Conjecture E.4](#A5.Thmtheorem4 "Conjecture E.4 (Lower Bound for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, 𝑝>2). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale"),
though tight stretch alone does not imply high PoE. An earlier draft of
this paper claimed a self-contained proof of $`\Omega(k^{p-1})`$ via a
one-dimensional collinear construction, but that proof was incorrect: in
one dimension, threshold trees can replicate the optimal Voronoi
partition exactly (since Voronoi cells in $`\mathbb{R}^{1}`$ are
intervals), so no one-dimensional instance can yield $`\text{PoE}>1`$.
Constructing the right multi-dimensional instance for the tight lower
bound remains the key open problem.

###### Theorem E.5 (Hardness of Approximation for $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$, all $`p\geq 1`$).

For any $`p\geq 1`$, the best explainable $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ clustering is
hard to approximate better than $`(\nicefrac{{1}}{{2}}-o(1))\ln k`$
unless $`P=NP`$.

[Theorem E.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Theorem E.1 (Upper Bound for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, 𝑝>2). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")
is the main new result. For $`p>2`$, combining the upper bound with the
GJPS21 $`\Omega(k)`$ lower bound (which applies to all $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$
on the instances where $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ distances equal $`\ell_{1}`$
distances) gives $`k\leq\text{PoE}_{p}(k)\leq O(k^{p-1}\ln\ln k)`$. If
[Conjecture E.4](#A5.Thmtheorem4 "Conjecture E.4 (Lower Bound for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, 𝑝>2). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")
is confirmed, the price would be $`\Theta(k^{p-1})`$ up to iterated
logarithmic factors.

##### Summary of the landscape.

Combining our results with \[[7](#bibe.bib7), [6](#bibe.bib6)\], the
price of explainability for $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ clustering is:

| $`p`$ | Upper bound | Lower bound | Approx. hardness |
|----|----|----|----|
| $`p=1`$ ($`k`$-medians) | $`1+H_{k-1}`$ \[tight, GPSY23\] | $`(1-o(1))\ln k`$ \[GPSY23\] | $`(\nicefrac{{1}}{{2}}-o(1))\ln k`$ |
| $`p=2`$ ($`k`$-means) | $`O(k\ln\ln k)`$ \[GPSY23\] | $`\Omega(k)`$ \[GJPS21\] | $`(\nicefrac{{1}}{{2}}-o(1))\ln k`$ |
| $`p>2`$ | $`O(k^{p-1}\ln\ln k)`$ \[this work\] | $`\Omega(k)`$ \[GJPS21\]^(∗) | $`(\nicefrac{{1}}{{2}}-o(1))\ln k`$ \[corollary\] |

^(∗)We conjecture $`\Omega(k^{p-1})`$; the tight stretch bound
$`(k{-}1)^{p-1}`$
([Proposition E.16](#A5.Thmtheorem16 "Proposition E.16 (Tight Stretch). ‣ E.5 Stretch Tightness and Lower Bound Discussion ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale"))
supports this.

#### E.1.2 Technical Overview

##### The $`D_{p}`$ distribution.

For $`p=2`$, the key to the solo/bulk analysis in \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\] is
the $`D_{2}`$ distribution, which samples threshold cuts $`(i,\theta)`$
with probability proportional to the squared length of the interval
containing $`\theta`$. We define a generalized *$`D_{p}`$ distribution*
([Section E.3](#A5.SS3 "E.3 The 𝐷_𝑝 Distribution ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")):
intervals are sampled proportional to $`|b-a|^{p}`$, and $`\theta`$ is
drawn from a density proportional to $`\min(\theta-a,b-\theta)^{p-1}`$.
This ensures the separation probability satisfies
$`\Pr[\text{separates }\mathbf{0},{\bm{p}}]\leq 2^{p-1}\|{\bm{p}}\|_{p}^{p}/L_{p}`$
([Lemma E.10](#A5.Thmtheorem10 "Lemma E.10 (Separation Probability). ‣ Pseudo-distance and stretch. ‣ E.3 The 𝐷_𝑝 Distribution ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")),
generalizing the $`p=2`$ bound.

##### The $`\ell_{p}`$ stretch.

The *stretch* of a pair $`(x,y)`$ in a center set $`V`$ measures the
ratio $`\|x-y\|_{p}^{p}/d_{p}(x,y)`$, where $`d_{p}`$ is the
pseudo-distance defined via interval decompositions. A key new
observation
([Lemma E.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma E.8 (ℓ_𝑝 Stretch Bound). ‣ Pseudo-distance and stretch. ‣ E.3 The 𝐷_𝑝 Distribution ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale"))
is that the $`\ell_{p}`$ stretch satisfies $`s_{p}\leq(|V|-1)^{p-1}`$,
which follows from the power mean inequality
$`({\sum a_{j}})^{p}\leq\ell^{p-1}\sum a_{j}^{p}`$ applied to the
$`\ell`$ intervals in each dimension. For $`p=2`$ this recovers the
known bound $`s_{2}\leq k`$; for general $`p`$ it gives
$`s_{p}\leq k^{p-1}`$.

##### Generalized solo/bulk analysis.

Using the $`D_{p}`$ distribution and the stretch bound, we run the same
solo/bulk algorithm as \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\] with the solo threshold at
$`s_{p}(v)\geq|U_{v}|^{p-1}/\ln^{2}|U_{v}|`$. The bulk cost is
$`O(k^{p-1})`$
([Lemma E.12](#A5.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma E.12 (Bulk Cost). ‣ E.4.3 Bulk Cut Analysis ‣ E.4 Upper Bound: 𝑂(𝑘^{𝑝-1}⁢lnln𝑘) ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale"));
the close-pair threshold is set at $`\Delta_{p}/k^{2p}`$ (generalizing
$`\Delta_{p}/k^{4}`$ for $`p=2`$) to ensure
$`L_{p}^{\prime}\geq L_{p}/2`$ for all $`p\geq 2`$. The solo cost is
$`O(k^{p-1}\ln\ln k)`$
([Lemma E.15](#A5.Thmtheorem15 "Lemma E.15 (Solo Cost). ‣ E.4.4 Solo Cut Analysis ‣ E.4 Upper Bound: 𝑂(𝑘^{𝑝-1}⁢lnln𝑘) ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")).
The solo cost analysis uses a generalized stretch-vs-separation lemma
([Lemma E.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Lemma E.13 (Stretch-vs-Separation for ℓ_𝑝). ‣ E.4.4 Solo Cut Analysis ‣ E.4 Upper Bound: 𝑂(𝑘^{𝑝-1}⁢lnln𝑘) ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")),
proved via Hölder’s inequality, and an induction on the compressed tree.
A key technical point: for $`p>2`$, the induction uses the convexity
inequality $`n^{p-1}-(n-\sigma)^{p-1}\geq(p-1)(n/2)^{p-2}\sigma`$ (valid
for $`\sigma\leq n/2`$) to handle the nonlinear scaling of the
$`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ cost in the number of centers.

##### Lower bound.

We show that the $`\ell_{p}`$ stretch bound $`(k-1)^{p-1}`$ is tight by
constructing $`k`$ equally-spaced collinear centers
([Proposition E.16](#A5.Thmtheorem16 "Proposition E.16 (Tight Stretch). ‣ E.5 Stretch Tightness and Lower Bound Discussion ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")).
The tight stretch provides suggestive (but not conclusive) evidence for
the conjectured $`\Omega(k^{p-1})`$ lower bound, since tight stretch
alone does not imply high PoE (the collinear instance has tight stretch
but $`\text{PoE}=1`$). For $`p=2`$, the $`\Omega(k)`$ lower bound was
proved by \[[6](#bibe.bib6)\] using a multi-dimensional construction on
the Boolean hypercube; since $`\|x-y\|_{p}^{p}=\|x-y\|_{1}`$ on
$`\{0,1\}^{d}`$, the same instance gives $`\Omega(k)`$ for all
$`p\geq 2`$. Extending this to a tight $`\Omega(k^{p-1})`$ lower bound
for $`p>2`$ remains open; the key difficulty is constructing a
multi-dimensional instance where $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ distance ratios grow
with $`p`$.

##### Hardness.

[Theorem E.5](#A5.Thmtheorem5 "Theorem E.5 (Hardness of Approximation for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, all 𝑝≥1). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")
is a direct corollary of the Boolean-hypercube reduction
of \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\]: since all distances on $`\{0,1\}^{d}`$ satisfy
$`\|x-y\|_{p}^{p}=\|x-y\|_{1}`$ for all $`p\geq 1`$, the reduction is
norm-independent. The technical contribution here is the observation of
norm equivalence; the reduction machinery is entirely
from \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\].

#### E.1.3 Related Work

Explainable clustering was introduced by Dasgupta
et al. \[[3](#bibe.bib3)\]. Subsequent improvements by Gamlath
et al. \[[6](#bibe.bib6)\], Makarychev–Shan \[[10](#bibe.bib10)\], and
Esfandiari et al. \[[4](#bibe.bib4)\] achieved $`O(\ln k\ln\ln k)`$ for
$`k`$-medians. Gupta et al. \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\] settled $`k`$-medians
and nearly settled $`k`$-means. Charikar–Hu \[[2](#bibe.bib2)\] gave
dimension-dependent bounds for $`k`$-means that are near-optimal when
$`d=O(\ln k)`$. Makarychev–Shan \[[11](#bibe.bib11)\] studied the
bi-criteria setting, showing that larger trees can reduce cost.
Bandyapadhyay et al. \[[1](#bibe.bib1)\] and Laber \[[9](#bibe.bib9)\]
studied the computational complexity of finding good explainable
clusterings. GPSY23 stated that their $`k`$-means ideas extend to
$`\ell_{p}`$ norms for $`p\geq 2`$ and deferred the details to future
work. GJPS21 noted higher-$`\ell_{p}`$ generalizations as an open
direction (Section 6 of their NeurIPS paper). Neither published detailed
proofs for the $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ objective with $`p>2`$.

##### Distinction from $`\ell_{p}`$-norm $`k`$-medians.

The objective $`\sum_{{\bm{x}}}\|{\bm{x}}-\pi({\bm{x}})\|_{p}^{p}`$
studied here raises each coordinate difference to the $`p`$-th power.
This is distinct from $`k`$-medians under the $`\ell_{p}`$ *norm*,
$`\sum_{{\bm{x}}}\|{\bm{x}}-\pi({\bm{x}})\|_{p}`$, which has been
studied for general $`p`$ in recent work \[[8](#bibe.bib8)\]. The two
objectives differ substantially: for equally-spaced points, the
$`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ price grows as $`k^{p-1}`$ while the $`\ell_{p}`$-norm
price remains $`O(\ln k)`$.

### E.2 Preliminaries

##### Clustering.

Given $`\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d}`$, centers
$`\mathcal{U}=\{{\bm{\mu}}^{1},\ldots,{\bm{\mu}}^{k}\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d}`$,
and assignment $`\pi:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{U}`$, the $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$
cost is
$`\mathrm{cost}_{p}(\pi,\mathcal{U})=\sum_{{\bm{x}}\in\mathcal{X}}\|{\bm{x}}-\pi({\bm{x}})\|_{p}^{p}`$.

##### Threshold trees.

A threshold cut $`(i,\theta)`$ represents the halfspace
$`\{x_{i}\leq\theta\}`$. A threshold tree $`T`$ is a binary tree with
cuts at internal nodes; it partitions $`\mathbb{R}^{d}`$ into
axis-aligned boxes at its leaves. A tree $`T`$ *separates*
$`\mathcal{U}`$ if each leaf box contains exactly one center. Given such
a tree, each data point is assigned to the unique center in its leaf
box, defining $`\pi_{T}`$. An *explainable clustering* is one of the
form $`\pi_{T}`$ for some threshold tree $`T`$.

##### Price of explainability.

For a given instance $`(\mathcal{X},k,p)`$,
$`\text{PoE}_{p}(k)=\max_{\text{instances}}\frac{\text{optimal explainable }\ell_{p}^{p}\text{ cost}}{\text{optimal }\ell_{p}^{p}\text{ cost}}.`$

##### Closest point process.

By translation/scaling invariance and linearity of expectations, the
price of explainability for an algorithm $`\mathcal{A}`$ is at most
$`\alpha_{p,\mathcal{A}}(k)=\max_{U:|U|=k}f_{p,\mathcal{A}}(U)`$, where

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle f_{p,\mathcal{A}}(U):=\mathbb{E}[\|\widehat{{\bm{p}}}\|_{p}^{p}],`$ |  | (9) |

$`\widehat{{\bm{p}}}`$ is the center in the leaf containing the origin,
and $`\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}=1`$ for the closest center $`{\bm{p}}^{*}`$
to the origin (cf. \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\]).

### E.3 The $`D_{p}`$ Distribution

Given a set of centers $`V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d}`$ and $`p\geq 1`$, we
define a distribution $`D_{p}(V)`$ over threshold cuts.

##### Intervals.

For each dimension $`i`$ and the projections of points in $`V`$, let
$`\ell_{i}=\min_{v\in V}v_{i}`$ and $`u_{i}=\max_{v\in V}v_{i}`$. The
projections partition $`[\ell_{i},u_{i}]`$ into intervals
$`\mathcal{I}_{i}`$. Let
$`\mathcal{I}_{\text{all}}=\bigcup_{i}\{(i,[a,b]):[a,b]\in\mathcal{I}_{i}\}`$
and define
$`L_{p}(V)=\sum_{(i,[a,b])\in\mathcal{I}_{\text{all}}}|b-a|^{p}`$.

##### The distribution.

$`D_{p}(V)`$ first selects $`(i,[a,b])\in\mathcal{I}_{\text{all}}`$ with
probability $`|b-a|^{p}/L_{p}(V)`$, then picks $`\theta\in[a,b]`$ with
density

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle P_{a,b}^{(p)}(\theta):=\frac{p\cdot 2^{p-1}}{(b-a)^{p}}\cdot\min(\theta-a,b-\theta)^{p-1}.`$ |  | (10) |

###### Observation E.6.

The density integrates to $`1`$:
$`\int_{a}^{b}P_{a,b}^{(p)}(\theta)\,d\theta=1`$.

###### Proof.

$`\int_{a}^{b}\min(\theta-a,b-\theta)^{p-1}\,d\theta=2\int_{0}^{(b-a)/2}t^{p-1}\,dt=\frac{(b-a)^{p}}{p\cdot 2^{p-1}}`$.
∎

For $`p=1`$: $`P_{a,b}^{(1)}(\theta)=1/(b-a)`$, i.e., the uniform
distribution. For $`p=2`$:
$`P_{a,b}^{(2)}(\theta)=\frac{4}{(b-a)^{2}}\min(\theta-a,b-\theta)`$,
matching \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\].

###### Remark E.7.

The bound $`2^{p-1}\|{\bm{p}}\|_{p}^{p}/L_{p}`$ can exceed $`1`$ for
some instances when $`p\geq 2`$; in such cases the bound is vacuous as a
probability but still valid. This does not affect the algorithm: the
separation probability bound is used in the cost analysis to bound the
expected cost per cut, not as a standalone probability estimate.

##### Pseudo-distance and stretch.

For $`{\bm{x}},{\bm{y}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}`$, define the $`\ell_{p}`$
pseudo-distance
$`d_{p}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})=\sum_{(i,[a,b])\in\mathcal{I}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})}|b-a|^{p}`$,
where
$`\mathcal{I}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})=\bigcup_{i}\{(i,[a,b]):[a,b]\in\mathcal{I}_{i}(x_{i},y_{i})\}`$.
Define the *$`\ell_{p}`$ stretch* of a pair $`{\bm{x}},{\bm{y}}\in V`$
as
$`s_{p}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})=\|{\bm{x}}-{\bm{y}}\|_{p}^{p}/d_{p}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})`$.

###### Lemma E.8 ($`\ell_{p}`$ Stretch Bound).

For any pair $`{\bm{x}},{\bm{y}}`$ in a set $`V`$ of $`k`$ points,
$`s_{p}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})\leq(k-1)^{p-1}`$.

###### Proof.

In each dimension $`i`$, let $`a_{1}^{i},\ldots,a_{\ell_{i}}^{i}`$ be
the interval lengths between $`x_{i}`$ and $`y_{i}`$. Then
$`|x_{i}-y_{i}|=\sum_{j}a_{j}^{i}`$ and the pseudo-distance contribution
is $`\sum_{j}(a_{j}^{i})^{p}`$. By the power mean inequality (convexity
of $`t\mapsto t^{p}`$ for $`p\geq 1`$):
$`\left(\sum_{j}a_{j}^{i}\right)^{p}\leq\ell_{i}^{p-1}\cdot\sum_{j}(a_{j}^{i})^{p}.`$
Since each $`\ell_{i}\leq k-1`$, summing over $`i`$:
$`\|{\bm{x}}-{\bm{y}}\|_{p}^{p}=\sum_{i}|x_{i}-y_{i}|^{p}\leq(k-1)^{p-1}\sum_{i}\sum_{j}(a_{j}^{i})^{p}=(k-1)^{p-1}\cdot d_{p}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}}).`$
∎

###### Remark E.9.

For $`p=1`$: $`s_{1}\leq 1`$, so $`\ell_{1}`$ distance equals cut-metric
distance. For $`p=2`$: $`s_{2}\leq k-1`$, recovering the known bound.
The bound is tight: $`k`$ equally-spaced points on a line give stretch
$`(k-1)^{p-1}`$.

###### Lemma E.10 (Separation Probability).

For any $`{\bm{p}}\in V`$,
$`\Pr_{(i,\theta)\sim D_{p}(V)}[\text{separates }\mathbf{0},{\bm{p}}]\leq 2^{p-1}\cdot\|{\bm{p}}\|_{p}^{p}/L_{p}(V)`$.

###### Proof.

The probability is
$`\sum_{i}\sum_{[a,b]\in\mathcal{I}_{i}}\frac{|b-a|^{p}}{L_{p}}\int_{a}^{b}P_{a,b}^{(p)}(\theta)\cdot\mathbbm{1}[\theta\text{ between }0,p_{i}]\,d\theta`$.
Using $`\min(\theta-a,b-\theta)^{p-1}\leq|p_{i}-\theta|^{p-1}`$ when
$`\theta`$ is between $`0`$ and $`p_{i}`$ (since $`p_{i}`$ lies at an
interval boundary), this is at most
$`\frac{p\cdot 2^{p-1}}{L_{p}}\sum_{i}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|p_{i}-\theta|^{p-1}\cdot\mathbbm{1}[\theta\text{ between }0,p_{i}]\,d\theta=\frac{p\cdot 2^{p-1}}{L_{p}}\sum_{i}\frac{|p_{i}|^{p}}{p}=\frac{2^{p-1}\|{\bm{p}}\|_{p}^{p}}{L_{p}}`$.
∎

### E.4 Upper Bound: $`O(k^{p-1}\ln\ln k)`$

We generalize the solo/bulk framework of \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\] to
$`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ for $`p\geq 2`$.

#### E.4.1 Definitions

For a subset $`V\subseteq U`$:

- •
  $`\Delta_{p}(V)=\max_{{\bm{x}},{\bm{y}}\in V}\|{\bm{x}}-{\bm{y}}\|_{p}^{p}`$
  is the $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ diameter.
- •
  A pair $`{\bm{x}},{\bm{y}}`$ is *far* if
  $`\|{\bm{x}}-{\bm{y}}\|_{p}^{p}\geq\Delta_{p}(V)/2`$, and *close* if
  $`\|{\bm{x}}-{\bm{y}}\|_{p}^{p}<\Delta_{p}(V)/k^{2p}`$.
- •
  $`s_{p}(V)=\max_{\text{far pairs}}s_{p}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})`$ is the
  stretch of the set.

##### Restricted distributions.

We use two restricted variants of $`D_{p}`$:

- •
  $`D_{p}^{\prime}(V)`$ is the distribution $`D_{p}(V)`$ restricted to
  intervals that are *not* between close pairs. Formally, we remove all
  intervals $`[a,b]`$ such that $`a`$ and $`b`$ are projections of
  centers $`{\bm{x}},{\bm{y}}`$ with
  $`\|{\bm{x}}-{\bm{y}}\|_{p}^{p}<\Delta_{p}/k^{2p}`$, and renormalize.
  Define
  $`L_{p}^{\prime}(V)=\sum_{(i,[a,b])\in\mathcal{I}^{\prime}}|b-a|^{p}`$
  where $`\mathcal{I}^{\prime}`$ is the restricted set.
- •
  $`D_{p}^{\prime\prime}(V;{\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})`$ is the distribution
  $`D_{p}(V)`$ conditioned on the sampled cut separating $`{\bm{p}}`$
  from $`{\bm{q}}`$. Equivalently, we restrict to intervals $`[a,b]`$
  such that $`\theta\in[a,b]`$ places $`{\bm{p}}`$ and $`{\bm{q}}`$ on
  opposite sides, and renormalize.

#### E.4.2 The Algorithm

Given a node $`v`$ with center subset $`U_{v}`$:

1.  1.
    Solo cut: If $`s_{p}(v)\geq|U_{v}|^{p-1}/\ln^{2}|U_{v}|`$, pick a
    far pair $`({\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})`$ of maximal stretch, sample
    $`(i,\theta)\sim D_{p}^{\prime\prime}(v;{\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})`$, apply
    the cut, and recurse on both children.
2.  2.
    Bulk cuts: Otherwise, repeatedly sample
    $`(i,\theta)\sim D_{p}^{\prime}(v)`$ and apply each sampled cut to
    the tree. Continue until all far pairs are separated. The resulting
    sequence of $`D_{p}^{\prime}`$ cuts forms a subtree at $`v`$;
    recurse on each leaf of this subtree.

We analyze the cost via a compressed tree $`T^{\prime}`$ with solo and
bulk nodes.

###### Remark E.11.

The algorithm prescribes a specific tree-building process: bulk cuts are
accumulated (each sampled $`D_{p}^{\prime}`$ cut is retained in the
tree) until all far pairs are separated. An implementation that discards
the sampled bulk cuts and replaces them with alternative splits would
yield a different tree from the one analyzed here.

#### E.4.3 Bulk Cut Analysis

###### Lemma E.12 (Bulk Cost).

The expected $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ cost increase due to all bulk cuts is
$`O(k^{p-1})\cdot\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}`$.

###### Proof.

At a bulk node $`v`$, the stretch satisfies
$`s_{p}(v)<|U_{v}|^{p-1}/\ln^{2}|U_{v}|`$. Let $`n=|U_{v}|`$.

*Step 1: $`L_{p}^{\prime}(v)\geq L_{p}(v)/2`$.* Each close pair
$`({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})`$ satisfies
$`\|{\bm{x}}-{\bm{y}}\|_{p}^{p}<\Delta_{p}/k^{2p}`$. The close-pair
intervals associated with pair $`({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})`$ across *all*
dimensions have total weight at most $`\|{\bm{x}}-{\bm{y}}\|_{p}^{p}`$,
because $`\sum_{j}|x_{j}-y_{j}|^{p}=\|{\bm{x}}-{\bm{y}}\|_{p}^{p}`$
already accounts for all coordinate contributions (dimension-free). With
at most $`\binom{k}{2}`$ close pairs, the total removed weight is at
most

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\binom{k}{2}\cdot\frac{\Delta_{p}}{k^{2p}}\;\leq\;\frac{\Delta_{p}}{2k^{2p-2}}.
``` |  |

Since
$`L_{p}(v)\geq\Delta_{p}(v)/s_{p}(v)\geq\Delta_{p}\ln^{2}n/n^{p-1}`$, we
need $`\Delta_{p}/(2k^{2p-2})\leq L_{p}(v)/2`$, i.e.,
$`n^{p-1}/k^{2(p-1)}\leq\ln^{2}n`$. For $`n\geq 3`$: since $`n\leq k`$,
$`n^{p-1}/k^{2(p-1)}\leq k^{p-1}/k^{2(p-1)}=1/k^{p-1}\leq 1\leq\ln^{2}n`$.
(For $`n=2`$, the bulk phase requires at most one cut with cost
$`O(\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p})`$, so the bound is immediate.) Therefore
$`L_{p}^{\prime}(v)\geq L_{p}(v)/2`$.

*Note:* The close-pair threshold $`\Delta_{p}/k^{2p}`$ generalizes the
$`\Delta_{p}/k^{4}`$ threshold used in \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\] for $`p=2`$
(where $`k^{2p}=k^{4}`$). The stronger threshold is needed for $`p>2`$
because $`L_{p}(v)`$ scales as $`\Delta_{p}/n^{p-1}`$ rather than
$`\Delta_{p}/n`$.

*Step 2: Expected number of bulk cuts.* Each bulk cut from
$`D_{p}^{\prime}`$ separates a far pair $`({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})`$ with
probability $`d_{p}^{\prime}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})/L_{p}^{\prime}(v)`$,
where $`d_{p}^{\prime}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})`$ is the pseudo-distance
computed over the *surviving* intervals only (those not removed as
close-pair intervals). We claim
$`d_{p}^{\prime}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})\geq d_{p}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})/2`$ for
every far pair.

*Proof of claim:* The total weight of all close-pair intervals is at
most $`\Delta_{p}/(2k^{2p-2})`$ (computed in Step 1). Since
$`({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})`$ is a far pair,
$`\|{\bm{x}}-{\bm{y}}\|_{p}^{p}\geq\Delta_{p}/2`$, so
$`d_{p}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})=\|{\bm{x}}-{\bm{y}}\|_{p}^{p}/s_{p}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})\geq(\Delta_{p}/2)/(n-1)^{p-1}\geq\Delta_{p}/(2k^{p-1}).`$
The removed mass attributed to $`({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})`$ is at most
$`\Delta_{p}/(2k^{2p-2})`$. Using the lower bound
$`d_{p}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})\geq\Delta_{p}/(2k^{p-1})`$, this removed mass
satisfies

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\frac{\Delta_{p}}{2k^{2p-2}}\;=\;\frac{\Delta_{p}/(2k^{p-1})}{k^{p-1}}\;\leq\;\frac{d_{p}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})}{k^{p-1}}.
``` |  |

Therefore

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
d_{p}^{\prime}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})\;\geq\;d_{p}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})-\frac{d_{p}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})}{k^{p-1}}\;=\;d_{p}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})\Bigl(1-\frac{1}{k^{p-1}}\Bigr)\;\geq\;\frac{d_{p}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})}{2},
``` |  |

where the last inequality uses $`k^{-(p-1)}\leq 1/2`$ for
$`k\geq 2,p\geq 2`$.

Therefore each bulk cut separates $`({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})`$ with
probability at least
$`d_{p}({\bm{x}},{\bm{y}})/(2L_{p}^{\prime}(v))\geq(\Delta_{p}/(4s_{p}))/L_{p}^{\prime}(v)`$.
There are at most $`\binom{n}{2}`$ far pairs. By a coupon-collector
argument (as in \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\]), the expected number of bulk cuts
is at most
$`O(s_{p}(v)\cdot L_{p}^{\prime}(v)/\Delta_{p}(v)\cdot\ln n)`$.

*Step 3: Cost per bulk cut.* Each bulk cut from $`D_{p}^{\prime}`$ costs
at most
$`2^{p-1}\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}\cdot 2^{p}\Delta_{p}(v)/L_{p}^{\prime}(v)`$
in expectation (by the separation probability lemma applied to the
origin; the $`2^{p}\Delta_{p}`$ factor bounds
$`\max_{{\bm{\mu}}\in U}\|{\bm{\mu}}\|_{p}^{p}`$ using the preprocessing
assumption $`\Delta_{p}\geq 1`$, as in
[Lemma E.14](#A5.Thmtheorem14 "Lemma E.14 (Solo Ratio). ‣ E.4.4 Solo Cut Analysis ‣ E.4 Upper Bound: 𝑂(𝑘^{𝑝-1}⁢lnln𝑘) ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")).
The product is
$`O(\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}\cdot\Delta_{p}(v)/L_{p}^{\prime}(v))`$
since $`2^{p-1}\cdot 2^{p}=O_{p}(1)`$ is a constant depending only on
$`p`$.

*Step 4: Total bulk cost at node $`v`$.* By Wald’s equation, the
expected cost at $`v`$ is (number of cuts) $`\times`$ (cost per cut):
$`O(s_{p}(v)\ln n)\cdot 2^{p}\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}.`$ For bulk nodes,
$`s_{p}(v)\leq n^{p-1}/\ln^{2}n`$, so the cost per node is
$`O(n^{p-1}/\ln n)\cdot\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}`$.

*Step 5: Summing over levels.* The logarithmic overlap lemma
of \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\] (specifically, their Lemma on compressed-tree
interval participation: each interval $`[c^{i}_{j},c^{i}_{j+1}]`$
participates as a threshold candidate in at most $`O(\ln k)`$ levels of
the compressed threshold tree) applies identically here. The key
structural hypothesis is that the tree has depth $`O(\ln k)`$ and each
node’s interval set is determined by the point projections at that
node—both properties hold regardless of $`p`$. Summing over all bulk
nodes:
$`O(k^{p-1}/\ln k)\cdot O(\ln k)\cdot\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}=O(k^{p-1})\cdot\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}`$.
∎

#### E.4.4 Solo Cut Analysis

###### Lemma E.13 (Stretch-vs-Separation for $`\ell_{p}`$).

For a far pair $`{\bm{p}},{\bm{q}}`$ in $`V`$ with $`|V|=n`$ and stretch
$`s_{p}=s_{p}({\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})`$, if we sample
$`(i,\theta)\sim D_{p}^{\prime\prime}(V;{\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})`$, the
expected number of centers on the smaller side of the cut is at least

|     |                                                       |     |
|-----|-------------------------------------------------------|-----|
|     |
       ``` math
       \sigma\;\geq\;\frac{s_{p}}{C_{p}\cdot A_{p}(n)^{p-1}}
       ```                                                    |     |

where $`A_{p}(n)=2\sum_{j=1}^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}j^{-1/(p-1)}`$ and
$`C_{p}`$ depends only on $`p`$. For $`p=2`$:
$`A_{2}(n)=\Theta(\ln n)`$, so $`\sigma\geq\Omega(s_{2}/\ln n)`$. For
$`p>2`$: $`A_{p}(n)=\Theta(n^{(p-2)/(p-1)})`$, so
$`\sigma\geq\Omega(s_{p}/n^{p-2})`$.

###### Proof.

*Step 1: Reduction to one dimension.* As in \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\], we
analyze the expected balance dimension by dimension and aggregate. In
dimension $`i`$, let $`c_{1}^{i}<c_{2}^{i}<\cdots<c_{m_{i}}^{i}`$ be the
sorted projections of $`V`$ onto coordinate $`i`$. Under
$`D_{p}^{\prime\prime}(V;{\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})`$, dimension $`i`$ is
selected with probability
$`d_{p}^{(i)}({\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})/d_{p}({\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})`$, where
$`d_{p}^{(i)}`$ is the pseudo-distance contribution from
dimension $`i`$. Let $`\bar{\sigma}_{i}`$ denote the expected balance
when dimension $`i`$ is selected. The overall expected balance is the
weighted average

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\bar{\sigma}\;=\;\sum_{i}\frac{d_{p}^{(i)}({\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})}{d_{p}({\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})}\cdot\bar{\sigma}_{i}.
``` |  |

Below we prove that the one-dimensional bound
$`\bar{\sigma}_{i}\geq s_{p}^{(i)}/A_{p}(m_{i})^{p-1}`$ holds for each
dimension, where
$`s_{p}^{(i)}=|p_{i}-q_{i}|^{p}/d_{p}^{(i)}({\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})`$ is the
per-dimension stretch and $`m_{i}\leq n-1`$. Since
$`A_{p}(m_{i})\leq A_{p}(n)`$ (as $`m_{i}\leq n-1`$), we obtain

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\bar{\sigma}\;\geq\;\frac{1}{A_{p}(n)^{p-1}}\sum_{i}\frac{d_{p}^{(i)}}{d_{p}}\cdot s_{p}^{(i)}\;=\;\frac{1}{A_{p}(n)^{p-1}}\cdot\frac{\sum_{i}|p_{i}-q_{i}|^{p}}{d_{p}({\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})}\;=\;\frac{s_{p}({\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})}{A_{p}(n)^{p-1}},
``` |  |

using
$`\sum_{i}(d_{p}^{(i)}/d_{p})\cdot s_{p}^{(i)}=\sum_{i}|p_{i}-q_{i}|^{p}/d_{p}=s_{p}`$.

*Step 2: One-dimensional analysis.* Fix a dimension and drop the
superscript. Suppose $`{\bm{p}}`$ and $`{\bm{q}}`$ are separated by
$`\ell`$ intervals with lengths $`a_{1},\ldots,a_{\ell}`$ (so
$`\ell\leq n-1`$). The $`D_{p}`$ distribution weights interval $`j`$
with $`w_{j}=a_{j}^{p}/S`$ where $`S=\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}a_{j}^{p}`$. A cut
in interval $`j`$ places $`\min(j,\ell+1-j)`$ centers on the smaller
side. Define $`\sigma_{j}=\min(j,\ell+1-j)`$. The expected balance is
$`\bar{\sigma}=\sum_{j}w_{j}\sigma_{j}`$.

*Step 3: Lower bound via Hölder’s inequality.* We prove directly that
$`\bar{\sigma}\geq s_{p}/A^{p-1}`$ where
$`A=\sum_{j}\sigma_{j}^{-1/(p-1)}`$. Apply Hölder’s inequality to
$`\sum_{j}a_{j}=\sum_{j}(a_{j}\sigma_{j}^{1/p})\cdot\sigma_{j}^{-1/p}`$
with exponents $`p`$ and $`p/(p-1)`$:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\sum_{j}a_{j}\;\leq\;\Bigl(\sum_{j}\sigma_{j}\,a_{j}^{p}\Bigr)^{1/p}\cdot\Bigl(\sum_{j}\sigma_{j}^{-1/(p-1)}\Bigr)^{(p-1)/p}.
``` |  |

Raising both sides to the $`p`$-th power:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Bigl(\sum_{j}a_{j}\Bigr)^{p}\;\leq\;\Bigl(\sum_{j}\sigma_{j}\,a_{j}^{p}\Bigr)\cdot A^{p-1}.
``` |  |

Therefore

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\bar{\sigma}\;=\;\frac{\sum_{j}\sigma_{j}\,a_{j}^{p}}{\sum_{j}a_{j}^{p}}\;\geq\;\frac{(\sum_{j}a_{j})^{p}}{A^{p-1}\cdot\sum_{j}a_{j}^{p}}\;=\;\frac{s_{p}}{A^{p-1}}.
``` |  |

This holds for *all* choices of $`a_{j}>0`$, with no Lagrangian or sign
assumptions on multipliers.

*Step 4: Bounding $`A`$.* Since $`\sigma_{j}=\min(j,\ell+1-j)`$ and
$`\ell\leq n-1`$:
$`A=\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\min(j,\ell+1-j)^{-1/(p-1)}\leq 2\sum_{j=1}^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}j^{-1/(p-1)}=A_{p}(n).`$

For $`p>2`$: $`1/(p-1)<1`$, so
$`\sum_{j=1}^{m}j^{-1/(p-1)}\leq\frac{(p-1)}{(p-2)}m^{(p-2)/(p-1)}`$,
giving $`A_{p}(n)=O(n^{(p-2)/(p-1)})`$ and
$`A_{p}(n)^{p-1}=O(n^{p-2})`$.

For $`p=2`$: $`1/(p-1)=1`$, so
$`A_{2}(n)=2H_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}=O(\ln n)`$.

*Step 5: Conclusion.* Therefore
$`\bar{\sigma}\geq s_{p}/A_{p}(n)^{p-1}`$, which gives
$`\sigma\geq\Omega(s_{p}/n^{p-2})`$ for $`p>2`$ and
$`\sigma\geq\Omega(s_{2}/\ln n)`$ for $`p=2`$. ∎

###### Lemma E.14 (Solo Ratio).

For a solo node $`v`$ with $`n=|U_{v}|`$ centers and far-pair stretch
$`s_{p}=s_{p}(v)`$, the expected cost increase divided by the expected
balance satisfies:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\frac{\mathbb{E}[\text{cost increase}]}{\mathbb{E}[\sigma]}\;\leq\;C_{p}^{\prime}\cdot\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}\cdot s_{p}\cdot\frac{A_{p}(n)^{p-1}}{s_{p}}=C_{p}^{\prime}\cdot A_{p}(n)^{p-1}\cdot\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}.
``` |  |

###### Proof.

The expected cost increase when we sample from
$`D_{p}^{\prime\prime}(v;{\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})`$ is at most

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}[\text{cost}]\leq\frac{2^{p-1}\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}}{d_{p}({\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})}\cdot 2^{p}\Delta_{p}=O(s_{p})\cdot\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p},
``` |  |

where the first factor is the conditional probability of separating the
origin from $`{\bm{p}}^{*}`$ (under $`D_{p}^{\prime\prime}`$, the
unconditional probability $`2^{p-1}\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}/L_{p}`$ is
divided by the conditioning probability
$`d_{p}({\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})/L_{p}`$), the second factor bounds the cost
when separated: by the generalized triangle inequality,
$`\max_{{\bm{\mu}}\in U}\|{\bm{\mu}}\|_{p}^{p}\leq 2^{p-1}(\Delta_{p}+\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p})\leq 2^{p}\Delta_{p}`$
(using the preprocessing assumption
$`\Delta_{p}\geq\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}=1`$ from the main theorem
proof), and we use $`\Delta_{p}/d_{p}({\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})\leq 2s_{p}`$
since $`({\bm{p}},{\bm{q}})`$ is a far pair. By
[Lemma E.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Lemma E.13 (Stretch-vs-Separation for ℓ_𝑝). ‣ E.4.4 Solo Cut Analysis ‣ E.4 Upper Bound: 𝑂(𝑘^{𝑝-1}⁢lnln𝑘) ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale"),
$`\mathbb{E}[\sigma]\geq s_{p}/(C_{p}A_{p}(n)^{p-1})`$. Dividing:
$`\text{ratio}\leq O(s_{p})\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}/(s_{p}/(C_{p}A_{p}(n)^{p-1}))=O(A_{p}(n)^{p-1})\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}`$.
∎

###### Lemma E.15 (Solo Cost).

The expected cost increase due to solo cuts in the subtree at $`v`$ is
at most
$`C_{p}^{\prime\prime}\cdot|U_{v}|^{p-1}\cdot(1+2\ln\ln|U_{v}|)\cdot\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}`$.

###### Proof.

We proceed by strong induction on $`n=|U_{v}|`$. The base case
$`n\leq 2`$ is immediate (one solo cut suffices, with cost
$`O(\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p})`$).

For the inductive step, let $`v`$ be a solo node. The cut produces two
children; let $`w^{*}`$ be the child containing the origin. Let $`S`$
denote the *random* number of centers separated to the smaller side by
this cut (so $`S\geq 1`$, since the conditioned cut separates at least
the far pair). Define $`\sigma=\mathbb{E}[S]`$. The origin goes to a
side with at most $`n-S`$ centers.

*Step 1: Cost decomposition.* Conditioning on $`S`$ and applying the
inductive hypothesis to $`w^{*}`$ (which has at most $`n-S`$ centers,
with $`\ln\ln(n-S)\leq\ln\ln n`$):

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\text{total cost at }v]`$ | $`\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[\text{cost at this cut}]+\mathbb{E}[\text{cost in subtree at }w^{*}]`$ |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}[\text{cost at this cut}]+C_{p}^{\prime\prime}\cdot\mathbb{E}\bigl[(n-S)^{p-1}\bigr]\cdot(1+2\ln\ln n)\cdot\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}.`$ |  |

*Step 2: Required inequality.* For the induction to close at
$`C_{p}^{\prime\prime}n^{p-1}(1+2\ln\ln n)\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}`$, we
need:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}[\text{cost at this cut}]\;\leq\;C_{p}^{\prime\prime}\bigl[n^{p-1}-\mathbb{E}[(n-S)^{p-1}]\bigr](1+2\ln\ln n)\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}.
``` |  |

*Step 3: Pointwise convexity bound.* For $`p\geq 2`$, the function
$`t\mapsto t^{p-1}`$ is convex. By the mean value theorem, for each
realization of $`S`$ with $`1\leq S\leq n/2`$:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
n^{p-1}-(n-S)^{p-1}\;\geq\;(p-1)(n-S)^{p-2}\cdot S\;\geq\;(p-1)(n/2)^{p-2}\cdot S.
``` |  |

(The bound $`S\leq n/2`$ holds because $`S`$ is the number on the
*smaller* side.) Taking expectations:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
n^{p-1}-\mathbb{E}[(n-S)^{p-1}]\;\geq\;(p-1)(n/2)^{p-2}\cdot\sigma.
``` |  |

*Step 4: The ratio bound.* From
[Lemma E.14](#A5.Thmtheorem14 "Lemma E.14 (Solo Ratio). ‣ E.4.4 Solo Cut Analysis ‣ E.4 Upper Bound: 𝑂(𝑘^{𝑝-1}⁢lnln𝑘) ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale"),
$`\mathbb{E}[\text{cost at this cut}]\leq O(A_{p}(n)^{p-1})\cdot\sigma\cdot\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}`$.
For $`p>2`$: $`A_{p}(n)^{p-1}=O(n^{p-2})`$. The required inequality
becomes:
$`O(n^{p-2})\cdot\sigma\leq C_{p}^{\prime\prime}(p-1)(n/2)^{p-2}\cdot\sigma\cdot(1+2\ln\ln n)`$,
which holds for $`C_{p}^{\prime\prime}`$ sufficiently large (depending
only on $`p`$), since both sides are proportional to
$`\sigma\cdot n^{p-2}`$.

For $`p=2`$: $`A_{2}(n)^{1}=O(\ln n)`$. The required inequality becomes:
$`O(\ln n)\cdot\sigma\leq C_{2}^{\prime\prime}\cdot\sigma\cdot(1+2\ln\ln n)`$,
which *does not hold* for large $`n`$. However, for $`p=2`$ the analysis
of \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\] uses a sharper balance bound (their Lemma 5.3,
which employs a different Lagrangian with the
$`h(x)=x/(1+\ln(\alpha/x))`$ function) to achieve $`O(k\ln\ln k)`$. Our
generalization recovers $`O(k\ln\ln k)`$ at $`p=2`$ by invoking the
GPSY23 bound directly as the base case. For $`p>2`$, the above argument
gives a self-contained proof with a strictly stronger balance-to-ratio
relationship.

*Step 5: Conclusion.* Combining: for $`p>2`$, the induction closes with
$`\Phi(n)=C_{p}^{\prime\prime}n^{p-1}(1+2\ln\ln n)`$. At the root with
$`n=k`$: total solo cost
$`\leq O(k^{p-1}\ln\ln k)\cdot\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}`$. For $`p=2`$,
we invoke \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\] Theorem 1.2 to get $`O(k\ln\ln k)`$. ∎

#### E.4.5 Proof of [Theorem E.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Theorem E.1 (Upper Bound for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, 𝑝>2). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")

###### Proof of [Theorem E.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Theorem E.1 (Upper Bound for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, 𝑝>2). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale") ($`p>2`$).

By the closest point process reduction, it suffices to bound
$`f_{p}(U)=\mathbb{E}[\|\widehat{{\bm{p}}}\|_{p}^{p}]`$ with
$`\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}=1`$.

*Preprocessing: small-diameter case.* If $`\Delta_{p}(U)<1`$ (i.e.,
$`\Delta_{p}<\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}`$ in the normalized setting), then
for every center $`{\bm{\mu}}\in U`$, the generalized triangle
inequality gives
$`\|{\bm{\mu}}\|_{p}^{p}\leq 2^{p-1}(\|{\bm{\mu}}-{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}+\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p})\leq 2^{p-1}(\Delta_{p}+1)<2^{p}`$.
Therefore $`f_{p}(U)\leq 2^{p}=O(1)\leq O(k^{p-1}\ln\ln k)`$, so the
bound holds trivially regardless of the tree. We henceforth assume
$`\Delta_{p}(U)\geq 1`$; this assumption is used in the cost bounds of
[Lemmas E.12](#A5.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma E.12 (Bulk Cost). ‣ E.4.3 Bulk Cut Analysis ‣ E.4 Upper Bound: 𝑂(𝑘^{𝑝-1}⁢lnln𝑘) ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")
and [E.14](#A5.Thmtheorem14 "Lemma E.14 (Solo Ratio). ‣ E.4.4 Solo Cut Analysis ‣ E.4 Upper Bound: 𝑂(𝑘^{𝑝-1}⁢lnln𝑘) ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale").

*Main argument.* By the generalized triangle inequality for
$`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ (i.e.,
$`\|a+b\|_{p}^{p}\leq 2^{p-1}(\|a\|_{p}^{p}+\|b\|_{p}^{p})`$):

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\|\widehat{{\bm{p}}}\|_{p}^{p}\leq 2^{p-1}(\|\widehat{{\bm{p}}}-{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}+\|{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}).
``` |  |

The term $`\|\widehat{{\bm{p}}}-{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}`$ is bounded by
the total cost increase due to all cuts. By
[Lemma E.12](#A5.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma E.12 (Bulk Cost). ‣ E.4.3 Bulk Cut Analysis ‣ E.4 Upper Bound: 𝑂(𝑘^{𝑝-1}⁢lnln𝑘) ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")
(bulk: $`O(k^{p-1})`$) and
[Lemma E.15](#A5.Thmtheorem15 "Lemma E.15 (Solo Cost). ‣ E.4.4 Solo Cut Analysis ‣ E.4 Upper Bound: 𝑂(𝑘^{𝑝-1}⁢lnln𝑘) ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")
(solo: $`O(k^{p-1}\ln\ln k)`$), we get
$`\mathbb{E}[\|\widehat{{\bm{p}}}-{\bm{p}}^{*}\|_{p}^{p}]\leq O(k^{p-1}\ln\ln k)`$.
Therefore $`f_{p}(U)\leq O(k^{p-1}\ln\ln k)`$. ∎

### E.5 Stretch Tightness and Lower Bound Discussion

We first show that the stretch bound $`(k-1)^{p-1}`$ from
[Lemma E.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma E.8 (ℓ_𝑝 Stretch Bound). ‣ Pseudo-distance and stretch. ‣ E.3 The 𝐷_𝑝 Distribution ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")
is tight, then discuss the current state of unconditional lower bounds
for the price of explainability.

###### Proposition E.16 (Tight Stretch).

For any $`k\geq 2`$ and $`p\geq 1`$, there exist $`k`$ centers in
$`\mathbb{R}^{d}`$ with a pair achieving $`\ell_{p}`$ stretch exactly
$`(k-1)^{p-1}`$.

###### Proof.

Place $`k`$ centers at equally-spaced points on the real line:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
{\bm{\mu}}^{j}=\frac{j-1}{k-1}\cdot{\bm{e}}_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{d},\quad j=1,\ldots,k.
``` |  |

The centers are separated by $`k-1`$ intervals of equal length
$`\frac{1}{k-1}`$ in dimension 1. For any pair
$`{\bm{\mu}}^{i},{\bm{\mu}}^{j}`$ with $`i<j`$, the $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$
distance is
$`\|{\bm{\mu}}^{i}-{\bm{\mu}}^{j}\|_{p}^{p}=((j-i)/(k-1))^{p}`$, and the
pseudo-distance is
$`d_{p}({\bm{\mu}}^{i},{\bm{\mu}}^{j})=(j-i)\cdot(1/(k-1))^{p}`$. The
stretch is therefore

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
s_{p}({\bm{\mu}}^{i},{\bm{\mu}}^{j})=\frac{((j-i)/(k-1))^{p}}{(j-i)/(k-1)^{p}}=(j-i)^{p-1}.
``` |  |

For the pair $`({\bm{\mu}}^{1},{\bm{\mu}}^{k})`$: $`s_{p}=(k-1)^{p-1}`$,
matching the upper bound from
[Lemma E.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma E.8 (ℓ_𝑝 Stretch Bound). ‣ Pseudo-distance and stretch. ‣ E.3 The 𝐷_𝑝 Distribution ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale").
∎

##### Why one-dimensional constructions cannot prove $`\text{PoE}>1`$.

The collinear construction above achieves maximal stretch, but it does
*not* yield a lower bound on the price of explainability. In one
dimension, the Voronoi cells of any set of $`k`$ sorted centers are
intervals. A threshold tree can replicate this partition exactly by
placing thresholds at the midpoints of consecutive centers. Therefore,
for any one-dimensional instance and any data distribution, there exists
a threshold tree achieving $`\text{PoE}=1`$. Any lower bound on the
price of explainability must use a multi-dimensional construction where
the Voronoi cells are not axis-aligned rectangles.

##### Known lower bounds.

For $`p=2`$ ($`k`$-means), Gamlath et al. \[[6](#bibe.bib6)\] proved
$`\text{PoE}_{2}(k)\geq\Omega(k)`$ using a multi-dimensional
construction. Their construction uses points on the Boolean hypercube
$`\{0,1\}^{d}`$, where $`\|x-y\|_{p}^{p}=\|x-y\|_{1}`$ for all $`p`$
(since each coordinate difference is $`0`$ or $`1`$); consequently, the
same instance yields $`\text{PoE}_{p}(k)\geq\Omega(k)`$ for every
$`p\geq 2`$. However, this transfer gives only $`\Omega(k)`$, not
$`\Omega(k^{p-1})`$: extending the lower bound to $`\Omega(k^{p-1})`$
for $`p>2`$ would require a construction where the $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$
distance ratios grow with $`p`$, not one where all $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$
distances coincide with $`\ell_{1}`$ distances.

##### Status of the $`\Omega(k^{p-1})`$ conjecture.

We conjecture
([Conjecture E.4](#A5.Thmtheorem4 "Conjecture E.4 (Lower Bound for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, 𝑝>2). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale"))
that $`\text{PoE}_{p}(k)=\Omega(k^{p-1})`$ for all $`p>2`$. The evidence
is suggestive but indirect:

1.  1.
    The $`\ell_{p}`$ stretch bound $`(k-1)^{p-1}`$ is tight
    ([Proposition E.16](#A5.Thmtheorem16 "Proposition E.16 (Tight Stretch). ‣ E.5 Stretch Tightness and Lower Bound Discussion ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")),
    establishing that the *geometric potential* for $`\Omega(k^{p-1})`$
    cost ratios exists. However, tight stretch alone does not imply a
    high price of explainability (the collinear instance has tight
    stretch but $`\text{PoE}=1`$).
2.  2.
    The upper bound $`O(k^{p-1}\ln\ln k)`$ from
    [Theorem E.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Theorem E.1 (Upper Bound for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, 𝑝>2). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")
    shows that $`k^{p-1}`$ is the correct order of growth (up to
    iterated logarithmic factors) if the lower bound matches.
3.  3.
    For $`p=2`$, the $`\Omega(k)`$ lower bound \[[6](#bibe.bib6)\]
    matches $`(k-1)^{p-1}`$ with $`p=2`$.

Proving the conjecture would require constructing a multi-dimensional
instance where axis-aligned threshold trees are forced to assign some
data points to centers at $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ distance $`\Omega(k^{p-1})`$
times their optimal distance. This is the main open problem from our
work.

###### Remark E.17.

For $`p=2`$, the $`\Omega(k)`$ lower bound of \[[6](#bibe.bib6)\]
together with the $`O(k\ln\ln k)`$ upper bound (the GPSY23 base case,
[Corollary E.2](#A5.Thmtheorem2 "Corollary E.2 (Upper Bound for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, 𝑝=2). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale"))
gives $`\text{PoE}_{2}(k)=\Theta(k)`$ up to iterated logarithmic
factors. For $`p>2`$, we have
$`\Omega(k)\leq\text{PoE}_{p}(k)\leq O(k^{p-1}\ln\ln k)`$
([Theorem E.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Theorem E.1 (Upper Bound for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, 𝑝>2). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")),
where the $`\Omega(k)`$ lower bound follows because the GJPS21 instance
lies on $`\{0,1\}^{d}`$ and all $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ distances equal
$`\ell_{1}`$ distances there. Closing the gap between $`\Omega(k)`$ and
$`O(k^{p-1}\ln\ln k)`$ requires a genuinely $`p`$-dependent
multi-dimensional construction.

### E.6 Hardness of Approximation

###### Proof of [Theorem E.5](#A5.Thmtheorem5 "Theorem E.5 (Hardness of Approximation for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, all 𝑝≥1). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale").

The hitting-set reduction from \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\] constructs centers
and data points on the Boolean hypercube $`\{0,1\}^{d}`$. For any
$`{\bm{p}},{\bm{q}}\in\{0,1\}^{d}`$ and any $`p\geq 1`$:
$`\|{\bm{p}}-{\bm{q}}\|_{p}^{p}=\sum_{i}|p_{i}-q_{i}|^{p}=\sum_{i}|p_{i}-q_{i}|=\|{\bm{p}}-{\bm{q}}\|_{1},`$
since $`|p_{i}-q_{i}|\in\{0,1\}`$ and $`0^{p}=0`$, $`1^{p}=1`$.
Therefore, the $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ distances on this instance are identical
to $`\ell_{1}`$ distances, and the hardness reduction
of \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\] (which combines the hitting-set reduction with
Feige’s set cover hardness \[[5](#bibe.bib5)\]) applies verbatim. The
conclusion is: unless $`P=NP`$, no polynomial-time algorithm
approximates the best explainable $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ clustering better
than $`(\nicefrac{{1}}{{2}}-o(1))\ln k`$. ∎

### E.7 Discussion and Open Problems

We have developed a self-contained proof of the price of explainability
under $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ clustering for $`p>2`$, establishing an upper
bound of $`O(k^{p-1}\ln\ln k)`$
([Theorem E.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Theorem E.1 (Upper Bound for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, 𝑝>2). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")).
For $`p=2`$ the GPSY23 bound $`O(k\ln\ln k)`$ applies directly
([Corollary E.2](#A5.Thmtheorem2 "Corollary E.2 (Upper Bound for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, 𝑝=2). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")).
The hardness result $`(\nicefrac{{1}}{{2}}-o(1))\ln k`$ extends to all
$`p\geq 1`$ as a corollary of \[[7](#bibe.bib7)\].

##### Open problems.

1.  1.
    Prove $`\Omega(k^{p-1})`$ lower bound for $`p>2`$. This is the most
    important open problem from our work. The tight stretch bound
    $`(k-1)^{p-1}`$ and the matching upper bound $`O(k^{p-1}\ln\ln k)`$
    suggest $`\Omega(k^{p-1})`$, but a proof requires constructing a
    multi-dimensional instance where axis-aligned threshold trees cannot
    approximate the Voronoi partition. One-dimensional constructions
    provably cannot work
    ([Section E.5](#A5.SS5 "E.5 Stretch Tightness and Lower Bound Discussion ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")).
2.  2.
    Remove the $`\ln\ln k`$ factor. We conjecture that the price of
    explainability for $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ is exactly $`\Theta(k^{p-1})`$
    for all $`p\geq 2`$. Proving this would likely require new ideas
    beyond the solo/bulk framework.
3.  3.
    The regime $`1<p<2`$. Our formal theorem statements and proofs are
    restricted to $`p\geq 2`$. While the $`D_{p}`$ distribution and
    stretch bound are defined for all $`p\geq 1`$, the solo cost
    induction
    ([Lemma E.15](#A5.Thmtheorem15 "Lemma E.15 (Solo Cost). ‣ E.4.4 Solo Cut Analysis ‣ E.4 Upper Bound: 𝑂(𝑘^{𝑝-1}⁢lnln𝑘) ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale"))
    relies on the convexity of $`t\mapsto t^{p-1}`$, which holds only
    for $`p\geq 2`$. For $`1<p<2`$, the upper bound is at most
    $`O(k^{p-1}\ln\ln k)`$ if the induction can be adapted (e.g., using
    concavity of $`t^{p-1}`$ differently), but we do not claim this as a
    theorem. The lower bound for $`1<p<2`$ is only $`\Omega(\ln k)`$
    (from the $`\ell_{1}`$ hitting-set construction). Determining the
    correct order of growth for $`1<p<2`$ is an interesting open
    problem.
4.  4.
    Better approximation for $`\ell_{p}^{p}`$ clustering ($`p\geq 2`$).
    The hardness of approximation is $`(\nicefrac{{1}}{{2}}-o(1))\ln k`$
    for all $`p`$, which is much smaller than the price $`\Omega(k)`$.
    Better approximation algorithms may exist, especially for $`p>2`$.
5.  5.
    Experimental evaluation. A companion code repository implements the
    $`D_{p}`$-based algorithm and basic experiments. The code now
    implements the exact bulk-phase procedure (sampled
    $`D_{p}^{\prime}`$ cuts retained in the tree) and uses the correct
    $`D_{1}`$ distribution for random thresholds. However, the
    lower-bound module produces $`\text{PoE}=1.0`$ on the collinear
    instance (consistent with our corrected theory that one-dimensional
    constructions give $`\text{PoE}=1`$) and the experiments evaluate
    simple synthetic instances rather than adversarial multi-dimensional
    constructions. Evaluating the algorithm on real datasets and
    constructing adversarial test instances remain future work.

#### Limitations

All our bounds are worst-case. The stretch-vs-separation tradeoff
([Lemma E.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Lemma E.13 (Stretch-vs-Separation for ℓ_𝑝). ‣ E.4.4 Solo Cut Analysis ‣ E.4 Upper Bound: 𝑂(𝑘^{𝑝-1}⁢lnln𝑘) ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale"))
uses a Hölder-inequality lower bound that may not be tight; optimizing
the constants is left for future work. The lower bound remains the main
gap: we conjecture $`\Omega(k^{p-1})`$ for $`p>2`$ but can only prove
$`\Omega(k)`$ (from the $`p=2`$ result of \[[6](#bibe.bib6)\], which
transfers to all $`p`$ via norm equality on the Boolean hypercube). An
earlier draft claimed a self-contained proof via a one-dimensional
construction; that proof was incorrect, and the correct lower bound
requires a multi-dimensional instance that we have not yet found. For
$`p=2`$, the solo cost induction does not close with our Hölder balance
bound alone; we invoke the sharper GPSY23 analysis as a base case. The
genuinely new material is concentrated in the $`p>2`$ upper-bound proof
([Theorem E.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Theorem E.1 (Upper Bound for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, 𝑝>2). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale"));
the $`p=2`$ result
([Corollary E.2](#A5.Thmtheorem2 "Corollary E.2 (Upper Bound for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝, 𝑝=2). ‣ E.1.1 Our Results ‣ E.1 Introduction ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale")),
hardness theorem, and lower bound all rely on prior work. A companion
code repository implements the $`D_{p}`$-based algorithm with correct
bulk-phase cut retention and $`D_{1}`$-weighted random thresholds;
however, it does not yet include adversarial multi-dimensional test
instances for the lower bound. The separation probability bound
([Lemma E.10](#A5.Thmtheorem10 "Lemma E.10 (Separation Probability). ‣ Pseudo-distance and stretch. ‣ E.3 The 𝐷_𝑝 Distribution ‣ Appendix E The Price of Explainability for ℓ_𝑝^𝑝 Clustering ‣ Early Discoveries of Algorithmist I:Promise of Provable Algorithm Synthesis at Scale"))
can be vacuous (exceed $`1`$) for $`p\geq 2`$ on some instances; this is
noted in the text and does not affect correctness of the algorithm
analysis.
````
